problem: Let $I=[0,2]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}=[0,i]\times {-i}.$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$

feedback.problem: Let $I=[0,1]⊂R$ and ${X}_{i}={i}\times [0,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi i)].$ Which of the following represents ${⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the intersection of a family of indexed sets consists of those elements that belong to *all* the sets:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\,:\,x\in {A}_{k}\,\,\text{for all}\,\,k\in I}
$$

Let's now write down one of our indexed sets. For example, if $i=\frac{1}{2},$ we have 

$$
{X}_{1/2}={\frac{1}{2}}\times [0,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})]={\frac{1}{2}}\times [0,1]={(\frac{1}{2},k)\,:\,k\in [0,1]}.
$$

This represents a vertical line segment from the point $(\frac{1}{2},0)$ to the point $(\frac{1}{2},1)$ in the coordinate plane, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/2827c5b33e84aff775d8bcc7ca98492afb220dda3a52fec4166afaa4da187d66.png)

In general,

$$
{X}_{i}={i}\times [0,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi i)]={(i,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi k))\,:\,k\in [0,i]}
$$

is the vertical line segment from the point $(i,0)$ to the point $(i,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi i)).$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/5a108a3c0cdf37a072d135674b6ffdb3894b8c5ba142604ea7a434b0f42245f5.png)

There are no points that lie in all sets. Therefore, the intersection of the indexed sets is $∅,$ the empty set.
